name: MPATGM (Man-Portable Anti-Tank Guided Missile)

header.one_liner: India's indigenous man-portable fire-and-forget ATGM; DRDO R&D Establishment Pune design; ~2 km range; IIR seeker; tandem HEAT warhead; intended to replace Milan/Konkurs in Indian Army service.
header.maker: DRDO Research & Development Establishment (R&DE) Pune — design; Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL) — production

at_a_glance.OEM: DRDO R&D Establishment Pune — design; BDL — production

what_it_is.prose: The MPATGM (Man-Portable Anti-Tank Guided Missile) is an indigenous Indian fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile system designed by the DRDO Research & Development Establishment (R&DE) in Pune. It is India's answer to the need for a Javelin-class man-portable ATGM with imaging infrared (IIR) seeker-based fire-and-forget capability. The MPATGM weighs approximately 14.5 kg (missile + launcher tube), has a range of 70–2,000 m, and uses an IIR seeker for target lock-on and autonomous guidance after launch. The warhead is a tandem HEAT design capable of defeating explosive reactive armour (ERA). The system can be fired from a shoulder-mounted position or a tripod. The MPATGM is intended to supplement and eventually replace older ATGM systems like the Milan and Konkurs in Indian Army service. The system has undergone extensive trials and is in the procurement phase.

deployments_procurement.summary: The MPATGM is in the procurement phase following successful trials. No specific procurement quantity or value has been publicly confirmed. The system is intended for Indian Army infantry units.

faq.question: How does the MPATGM compare to the FGM-148 Javelin?
faq.answer: The MPATGM is India's indigenous answer to the Javelin-class fire-and-forget ATGM. Both use IIR seeker technology. The MPATGM has a range of ~2 km (vs ~4.7 km for Javelin) and a tandem HEAT warhead. The MPATGM is designed to be more cost-effective and suitable for Indian Army mass procurement.

faq.question: What is the status of the MPATGM programme?
faq.answer: The MPATGM has completed extensive trials and is in the procurement phase. The Indian Army has expressed interest in acquiring the system to supplement and eventually replace older ATGM systems like the Milan and Konkurs. No specific procurement quantity or value has been publicly confirmed.

faq.question: What is the Man-Portable Anti-Tank Guided Missile (MPATGM)?
faq.answer: MPATGM is a third-generation, fire-and-forget man-portable anti-tank guided missile developed by DRDO. It is designed for the soldier against armoured threats and features a top-attack capability, which the DRDO has demonstrated in successful flight trials against moving targets.

faq.question: Has MPATGM completed developmental trials?
faq.answer: DRDO has successfully conducted flight tests of the indigenously developed third-generation MPATGM, including tests demonstrating top-attack capability against moving targets, marking progress toward user trial validation and eventual induction.
